title: Match consistency to the cluster
summary: A consistency level tells Cassandra how many replicas must answer an operation.
introduction: A consistency level tells Cassandra how many replicas must answer an operation. Your task: Calculate the majority of three replicas.
learningObjectives: Calculate the majority of three replicas.
Explain the example for match consistency to the cluster

blocks.text: A consistency level tells Cassandra how many replicas must answer an operation. It only makes sense together with the replication setup.
Use a local single-node Cassandra 4+ practice cluster and cqlsh. The SimpleStrategy keyspace below is only for that local lesson. These commands do not run in this site's SQLite playground.

blocks.code:
Worked example with three replicas:
ONE needs one replica response.
QUORUM needs a majority: two responses.
The local course has only one replica, so it cannot demonstrate surviving multiple replica failures.
blocks.title: Match consistency to the cluster

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: A majority of three replicas means two acknowledgements.
The local one-replica exercise cannot demonstrate the availability of a real replicated cluster.

blocks.text: The example shows why a stronger response requirement can trade availability for stronger agreement.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Do not choose a production consistency policy from a one-node demo alone. Test failures with the actual replication layout.

blocks.text: Calculate the majority of three replicas.
